notes:
Summary: Stalled / closed-lost — LumenForge evaluated Redwood Dedicated and Private for a customer-facing edge chat/embeddings stack. After PoC showed parity on latency, the infra org elected to self-host using vLLM + Triton/TensorRT-LLM to reduce long-term per-token cost and retain kernel-level control.

Key quotes: "We can shave >40% off op-costs if we run optimized TensorRT clusters ourselves — board wants capital investment over recurring SaaS spend." — CTO (Ivan Korzun).

Reasoning: security and control + cost predictability. Security team objected to hosted secret rotation model; required HSM/KMS under customer control and strict retention/residency; legal insisted on no external model caching. The platform team also pushed for ability to compile custom kernels (TensorRT) and deep observability into GPU telemetry.

Internal dynamics: strong interest from product and ML infra teams initially, but CTO change in Dec led to pause; new infra lead favors on-prem dedicated infra. No clear champion in product org after head of AI moved to a new role.

Sales notes: AE (Maya) and SE (Carlos) did 3 calls + one on-site demo. PoC (Dec->Jan) completed: latency/throughput targets met on Redwood Dedicated pilot, cost analysis presented (see pricing deck). Procurement asked for 3rd-party code audit and longer retention SLA (12+ months) — Redwood could to some extent but requirement to host KMS on-customer blocked hosted option.

Outcome: Customer notified procurement decision 2026-01-28 — choosing in-house stack (vLLM + TGI/TensorRT-LLM) and open-source tuning for cost reasons. Marked closed-lost.

Follow-up plan: leave migration checklist + estimated delta analysis, share infra automation templates (k8s + Triton) as goodwill. Periodic check-ins: Q3 2026.
